explanations.positive_explanation: This feature detects the standard boilerplate header of source files—specifically the Apache License 2.0 copyright and licensing notice that appears at the top of code files.
explanations.negative_explanation: This feature detects the end-of-header or title line—i.e. the paragraph break or blank-line separator immediately following a section heading (headlines, menu labels, article titles, etc.) and before the main body text.

explanations.positive_explanation: This neuron lights up on broad, catch-all introducers—indefinite/wh-pronouns and related nouns (whatever, what, any, things, advantages, benefits, relevance, etc.)—that launch a generalizing or concessive clause or headline-style summary.
explanations.negative_explanation: The feature is a “section‐header/boilerplate” detector: it lights up on the markers and formatting that introduce or delimit structured metadata or front‐matter (comment-block stars, dashes and all-caps headings, license banners, legal case captions, biographical or contents headings, etc.).
